# Evaluation scope

State the question, teaching-case source, and limits of your review.

# Evidence and verification

List input files or table locations, checks performed, tools, formulas or commands, and software versions where relevant. Distinguish supplied outputs from results you reproduced.

# Findings

| Finding ID | Claim or decision | Judgment | Priority | Evidence location | Recommended action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F01 | | | | | |

Use Supported, Incorrect, Not established, or Not applicable. Priorities are Blocking, Major, Minor, or none when no correction is needed. Split mixed claims.

# Corrected conclusion

Write a short conclusion proportional to the evidence.

# Missing evidence and next actions

Prioritize specific requests and explain what each would resolve.

# Reproducibility and assistance

Record input versions, checksums or Git commit if available; environment details; and any assistance used. Identify synthetic teaching materials clearly.

# Reflection and revisions

Preserve your initial judgment. After self-review, explain what changed and why. State one skill to strengthen next.
